metadata.note: The Freehold and Jamesburg Agricultural Rail Road (NJ, chartered 1851, opened 1853) and its extensions - the Squankum & Freehold Marl Co. road Freehold - Farmingdale (1868) and the Farmingdale & Squan Village Farmingdale - Sea Girt extension (1872) - plus the C&A-built Monmouth Junction - Jamesburg connection (1866/67), and the same track as the Pennsylvania Railroad's Jamesburg Branch to the last passenger train on May 29 1962. One feature per drawable span x operator; Rule 4 splits share identical geometry. Research report: research/branches/freehold_and_jamesburg_agricultural_railroad.txt.
sources: https://digital.hagley.org/system/files/2026-03/mss_2915_00_02_prrchronology_<YEAR>.pdf -- PRR General Chronology (Christopher T. Baer, PRRT&HS / Hagley), years 1851-1865 and 1874-1885
research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt (Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952, Pennsylvania table 39) -- Trenton - Monmouth Junc. - Freehold - Sea Girt - Red Bank train, times legible

https://www.branchline.uk/jfpdf/newjerseyrrs.pdf -- John Fowler, New Jersey Railroads SL214 (10.06.25), line 65 'Jamesburg Branch (PRR) ex Freehold & Jamesburg RR': mileposts and 1875 timetable letter y
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freehold_Secondary -- Wikipedia (pointer only): June 1 1879 PRR operation citing the 1886 NJ Acts pp. 350-351; 1962 end; 1964 track removal
metadata.operator_split: Monmouth Jct - Jamesburg: Camden and Amboy June 1867 - Nov 30 1871, PRR from Dec 1 1871 (split at 1871). Jamesburg - Freehold (1853), Freehold - Farmingdale (1868) and Farmingdale - Sea Girt (1872): Freehold and Jamesburg to May 31 1879, PRR from June 1 1879 (split at 1879). The F&J was NOT part of the Dec 1871 PRR lease (United Companies declined to lease it in Dec 1870). Not treated as splits: C&A stock control and C&A-supplied rolling stock 1853-1855; the 1879 reorganization; Penn Central 1968 (freight only by then).
metadata.freight_only_audit: Nothing freight-only drawn (Rule 1). Excluded: Monmouth Jct - Jamesburg early 1866 - June 2 1867 ('freight service only until 1867'); everything after May 29 1962 (Penn Central / Conrail / Delaware & Raritan River freight on Monmouth Jct - Jamesburg - Freehold - Farmingdale); the Freehold Marl Company sidings at Farmingdale - Squankum (no passenger evidence).
metadata.horsecar_audit: Nothing trimmed (Rule 5): locomotive-worked from the first train (June 1853); the 1867 Monmouth Jct shuttle used a Grice & Long steam car.
omitted: [8] C&A (1867-1871) and PRR (1872-1879) through trains over the F&J track (Monmouth Jct - Freehold, Camden / West Philadelphia - Long Branch summer service): drawable NONE as a separate feature; the years are covered by the F&J features.
[9] Sea Girt - Long Branch over the New York & Long Branch, PRR trains from Oct 1875: another company's track, belongs to the NY&LB / North Jersey Coast Line layer; not drawn here.
Chartered but never built: F&J extension to Toms River (1852), Deans Pond - Six Mile Run (1853), PRR Manasquan - Long Branch (surveyed 1879).
not_yet_sourced: Operator 1853-1879 (the Rule 4 question): the F&J itself per the Dec 1870 no-lease decision, the 1872 'operated by' entry and the 1874 F&J running request; but the 1853 opening entry says 'controlled by the Camden & Amboy' with C&A rolling stock, and no primary statement of who ran the LOCAL trains 1872-1879 was found. If the F&J was PRR-run after the Dec 1871 lease, the 1879 splits would move to 1871.
June 1 1879 PRR operation rests on the 1886 NJ Acts, read only via Wikipedia. 1879 consolidation date May 21 vs May 24 (two Wikipedia articles) - does not affect drawn years.
Freehold - Farmingdale operator 1868-1872 is inferred (Apr 1 1868 running-rights act; Wikipedia 'leased to the F&J'), not stated. Opening Dec 28 1868 (Chronology compiler) vs Dec 19 (Valuation).
Farmingdale & Squan Village: Wikipedia says leased to the F&J in 1874; the Chronology has it operated by the F&J from its July 1872 opening. Drawn from 1872.
Year-round service 1869-1879 implied by the 1874 mail route and Fowler's 1875 timetable letter, not proven for every year (several entries concern summer through trains). Not used to trim.
headway_min everywhere and avg_speed_kmh before 1951 are estimates; only the Feb 1952 Guide was read for running times.

segments.note: The Freehold and Jamesburg Agricultural Rail Road, Jamesburg - Lower Jamesburg - Tracey - Englishtown - Manalapan (Tennent from 1879) - Battle Ground - Freehold, connecting at Jamesburg with the Camden and Amboy for South Amboy (boat to New York) and Bordentown. First locomotive June 16 1853; formal opening July 14 1853 and revenue passenger service from July 18 1853 (PRR Chronology, citing Ellis 1885) - steam from the first train, so Rule 5 trims nothing. The C&A supplied the rolling stock until Feb 1855 and held a large stock interest, but the F&J ran its own trains (own superintendent from 1854); in Dec 1870 the United Companies declined to lease it ('more remunerative ... under own management'), so it was not in the PRR's Dec 1 1871 lease. Ends 1879: the Pennsylvania Railroad operated the line from June 1 1879 (1886 NJ Acts, read only via Wikipedia) and the PRR feature on identical geometry begins there. Operator for 1853-1879 is medium confidence - see metadata.not_yet_sourced. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (the report's 2-4 trains each way a day is NOT SOURCED; no timetable frequency was counted).
sources: Segment-level: opening June 16 / July 14 / July 18 1853, C&A rolling stock to Feb 1855 and the Dec 1870 decision not to lease from the PRR General Chronology (Baer, PRRT&HS/Hagley) 1853, 1855 and 1870 entries; June 1 1879 PRR operation from Wikipedia Freehold Secondary citing the 1886 NJ Acts (Acts not read). Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Monmouth Junction (Deans Pond) - Dayton - Jamesburg, built by the Camden and Amboy under the F&J's charter and operated by the C&A under the Joint Companies' lease of Sep 15 1865. Opened early 1866 but 'used for freight service only until 1867', so 1866 is not drawn (Rule 1). C&A revenue passenger service began June 3 1867 with a Grice & Long steam car (mechanical, not Rule 5), and from Oct 1 1867 trains ran through from Monmouth Jct to Freehold. Ends 1871: the PRR took over all C&A operation on Dec 1 1871; the PRR feature on identical geometry begins there. Deeded to the United New Jersey RR & Canal Co. July 29 1874. headway_min is an ESTIMATE (the report's 2-4 trains each way a day is NOT SOURCED; no timetable frequency was counted).
sources: Segment-level: freight-only 1866, June 3 1867 passenger start and Oct 1 1867 through trains from the PRR General Chronology 1866 and 1867 entries (citing the Monmouth Democrat); Dec 1 1871 PRR operation from the Chronology 1871 entry. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Freehold - Howell - Fairfield - Yellow Brook - Farmingdale, the railroad of the Squankum & Freehold Marl Company, opened Dec 28 1868 (first day of revenue service per the PRR Chronology compiler; the Valuation says Dec 19, opening excursion Dec 26), connecting at Farmingdale with the Raritan & Delaware Bay for Long Branch. An NJ act of Apr 1 1868 let the F&J run over it, and Wikipedia says it was leased to the F&J that year; the F&J as operator is INFERRED from that act and the 1872 'operated by' entry for the next section, not stated outright for 1868-1872 (medium confidence). C&A summer through trains Camden - Long Branch ran over it from June 17 1869 and PRR ones from 1872; those are not drawn separately. Ends 1879 with PRR operation from June 1 1879 (1886 NJ Acts via Wikipedia). headway_min is an ESTIMATE (the report's 2-4 trains each way a day is NOT SOURCED; no timetable frequency was counted).
sources: Segment-level: Apr 1 1868 running-rights act, Dec 28 1868 opening and June 17 1869 through trains from the PRR General Chronology 1868 and 1869 entries (citing the Valuation, State Gazette, PL); 1868 lease and June 1 1879 PRR operation from Wikipedia Freehold Secondary. Operator for 1868-1872 inferred, not stated. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Farmingdale - Allaire - Allendale (Allenwood) - Squan (Manasquan from 1879) - Sea Girt, the Farmingdale & Squan Village Railroad, opened July 22 1872 and 'operated by Freehold & Jamesburg Agricultural Railroad' (PRR Chronology, citing the Monmouth Democrat and Valuation). From Oct 1875 PRR trains ran on from Sea Girt over the New York & Long Branch to Long Branch (not drawn here - another company's track), except in the 1879 season. A Jamesburg & Squan Village mail route existed from Jan 1874. Ends 1879 with PRR operation from June 1 1879 (1886 NJ Acts via Wikipedia). headway_min is an ESTIMATE (the report's 2-4 trains each way a day is NOT SOURCED; no timetable frequency was counted).

Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Monmouth Junction - Dayton - Jamesburg under Pennsylvania Railroad operation from Dec 1 1871 (lease of the United Companies; C&A/UNJ track). The usual routing of the Freehold - Sea Girt trains to Trenton (via Princeton Jct) and New York; in Feb 1952 the Trenton - Sea Girt - Red Bank train ran here (Guide table 39, times legible). segments.note: Freehold - Howell - Farmingdale - Allaire - Allenwood - Manasquan - Sea Girt under Pennsylvania Railroad operation from June 1 1879 (1886 NJ Acts via Wikipedia). Oct 1879 Squan renamed Manasquan; a new Manasquan station 1881. In Feb 1952 the trains ran on from Sea Girt over the NY&LB to Red Bank (that track is the North Jersey Coast Line layer's, not drawn here). Last passenger train May 29 1962, 'ending passenger service between Monmouth Jct. and Sea Girt'. Farmingdale - Sea Girt was torn up in 1964 (now partly the Edgar Felix Bikeway); Freehold - Farmingdale was reactivated for freight in 2023 - context, not drawn (Rule 1). headway_min is an ESTIMATE: about 2-3 trains each way on weekdays in 1951 from partly legible Official Guide columns; no other year's frequency was counted.
